title: Private VPC Deploy: Network Compatibility, Upgrade Safety, and Air-gap Acceptance Criteria
creator: Asha Patel
summary: Define unambiguous network, upgrade and air-gapped acceptance criteria so Private (VPC/on-prem) customers can validate deployability and upgrade safety without allowing unexpected egress or downtime. This document captures requirements, pass/fail gates, verification steps, telemetry, and rollout guidance for release owners and customer operations.
requirements: Network connectivity contract: list of allowed outbound hosts/IP ranges and ports for initial install, periodic health checks, and optional telemetry. Each required endpoint must include fallback behavior when unreachable.
Offline-only install mode: provide an operator-managed artifact bundle and signed manifest that can be installed without any outbound connectivity; installation must validate signatures locally.

Staged upgrade contracts: agent, control-plane, and node upgrades must support a two-phase process: preflight validation + apply. Preflight must be runnable in air-gapped environments with only local artifacts.
Maintenance window model: upgrades must be configurable with a maintenance window and a non-intrusive dry-run mode that simulates steps and reports resource/compatibility issues.
Rollback safety: upgrades must include an automated rollback trigger if >X% of p99 latency regressions or >Y% error increase are observed within Z minutes of rollout.
Minimal egress default: out-of-the-box configurations for Private must require zero egress; any enabled egress must be explicit and documented with customer-consent workflow.
Artifact provenance: all images/artifacts used for private deployments must be signed (cosign or equivalent) and checksummed; the operator must validate signatures prior to use.
KMS and key rotation: support customer-managed KMS integrations (cloud KMS/HSM) and a documented rotation workflow that does not require internet access when KMS is reachable within VPC.
Operational observability: release must provide a local diagnostics bundle and a telemetry-optional mode where metrics/logs are retained locally and exportable to customer telemetry endpoints.
RBAC and audit: support role separation for upgrade operators, with audit logs of all upgrade actions retained for configurable retention periods and exportable inside the VPC.
Compatibility matrix: clearly enumerate supported OS versions, container runtimes, kernel modules, and required node resources (GPU/CPU/memory) for each release tag.
Test harness: provide a customer-run validation script that runs basic smoke checks (control plane health, inference echo, artifact integrity) in both connected and disconnected modes.
Graceful degradation: define fallback behavior when optional services (e.g., usage telemetry, external model registry) are unavailable — core serving must remain functional.
Time synchronization: require NTP or equivalent; if network time is restricted, provide guidance for manual time skew detection and remediation.
Operator guidance: include a one-page runbook for common upgrade failure modes and recovery commands that are viable in air-gapped deployments.
out_of_scope: The hosted control plane operated by Redwood for non-enterprise customers (this doc covers private/VPC only)
Full automation for third-party third-party proxy configuration — we provide documented examples but not managed configs for every vendor.
Providing physical media distribution — we require signed bundle support, but sourcing physical media logistics is a customer concern.
Network appliance integrations beyond documented proxy and TLS termination patterns (specific vendor integrations are separate projects).
acceptance_criteria: Connectivity doc validated: QA-run checklist confirms that a fresh VPC with default-deny egress but allowing listed control-plane endpoints can install and report health within documented time bounds.
Signed-artifact offline install: operator successfully installs using a signed artifact bundle without outbound network access; signature verification must be enforced and documented.
Preflight pass/fail: preflight tool returns deterministic, human-readable failures for common misconfigurations (missing kernel modules, insufficient disk, port blocked).
Rollback trigger: Simulated rollout that induces a p99 latency regression triggers automated rollback within the configured SLA and leaves the cluster in a healthy serving state.
No-default-egress: default deployment settings must not open any outbound egress; telemetry-opt-in must be explicit and require a single command or UI toggle.
Maintenance-window respect: upgrades scheduled outside the maintenance window must not start; dry-run mode must complete without applying changes and produce a remediation plan.
Audit trail: all upgrade steps produce audit entries stored locally with timestamps and operator identity; exportable via documented CLI.
Artifact validation: checksum and signature checks are performed and logged; mismatch causes immediate abort with clear error messaging and remediation hints.
Air-gap verification script: customer-run verification script completes with pass/fail status and an attachments bundle (logs, system snapshot) when run in an isolated subnet.
Telemetry opt-in validation: when telemetry is opted-out, no outbound connections to Redwood telemetry endpoints are observed during acceptance tests.
Operator runbook accuracy: at least two independent operator engineers can follow the runbook to complete an upgrade and a rollback in a test lab environment within the documented time.
Release notes: release notes include a clear list of required network allowlists (IP, FQDN, ports), and a compatibility matrix for customer verification prior to upgrade.
Security review: product and engineering security sign-off is recorded, including KMS integration and artifact-signing verification steps.
Cluster-level health: post-upgrade smoke tests must validate routing, KV cache warmup, and an end-to-end inference request success rate >= 99% for baseline workload used in testing.
Supportability: support/SEs can reproduce the top 5 failure modes and have documented mitigation steps in the internal playbook.
verification_tests: Run install in isolated VPC with default-deny egress and allowed ports: verify successful bootstrap and agent-heartbeat frequency within documented bounds.
Perform offline bundle install: validate cosign signatures locally and ensure process fails on tampered artifact.
Execute preflight checks: intentionally misconfigure a required kernel parameter and confirm preflight reports the specific missing requirement.
Simulate upgrade-induced latency regression via traffic injector and verify rollback triggers and service continuity.
Toggle telemetry opt-in and use packet-capture in the node to assert no outbound telemetry when disabled.
Run the air-gap verification script and confirm generated attachment bundle contains expected artifacts (systemd journal excerpt, container runtime info, artifact checksums).
Validate RBAC: perform an upgrade attempt using a non-upgrade role and confirm action is denied and recorded in audit logs.
Resource exhaustion test: reduce available disk space to threshold and assert upgrade aborts with actionable error and cleanup guidance.
rollout_and_rollback_plan: Canary scope: default canary to 5% of nodes in a separate AZ with traffic drained and replayed to canary instances for X minutes before widening.
Preflight gating: preflight must succeed on canary subset before any control-plane or node group is upgraded.
Widening policy: progressive rollout in N steps with automated health checks and manual approval gates between steps.
Automatic rollback: health-check thresholds (latency/error) defined per release; failing thresholds trigger automatic rollback for the last successful revision.
Manual halt: operators can pause rollout and enter manual remediation mode; remediation steps documented in runbook.
Post-rollback validation: after rollback, run a degraded smoke test to ensure serving functionality and collect telemetry for incident review.
Customer notification: enterprise customers with private deployments will receive pre-upgrade advisories, maintenance window confirmations, and a post-upgrade report.
monitoring_and_telemetry: Local metrics: provide a standardized local metrics endpoint and scraping guidance for customer Prometheus instances.
Health checks: implement explicit upgrade-phase health metrics (preflight_ok, upgrade_in_progress, upgrade_success, upgrade_rollback).
Diagnostic bundle: built-in CLI command to collect a time-bounded diagnostic bundle for support, optimized for minimal egress when exported.
Alerting: default rule set for critical upgrade failures and p99 latency spikes with recommended thresholds and runbook links.
Privacy mode: when telemetry is disabled, metrics are stored only locally and exports are disabled by default.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Require artifact signing by default: reduces risk for air-gapped installs at the cost of additional CI complexity to sign bundles.
Default to zero-egress: improves security posture but increases support burden for customers who need to opt into telemetry or hosted registries.
Two-phase upgrades: preflight step increases time-to-upgrade but materially reduces failed upgrade blast radius in constrained networks.
Conservative canary size: smaller canary preserves safety for highly regulated customers but increases time to fully roll out fixes.
open_questions: What is the maximum acceptable time-to-install for offline bundle installs before classifying as a poor UX (goal: < 60 minutes)?
Should we support a Redwood-hosted air-gap artifact mirror appliance as a premium offering?
How granular should the allowlist be (FQDN vs. IP ranges) given customers run private DNS or split-horizon setups?
Should we require local time synchronization enforcement during preflight or merely warn when skew exceeds threshold?
notes: This ticket synthesizes findings from customer pilots in Q4-2025 where customers with strict egress controls experienced ambiguous upgrade failures. Next steps: align with ENG for preflight implementation, schedule security review, and validate offline bundle process with two pilot customers.
